babs.1: When one finds neither water nor earth
babs.2: Tayammum when resident, if one finds no water and fears missing the prayer
babs.3: Does the one performing tayammum blow on his hands?
babs.4: Tayammum for the face and hands
babs.5: Clean earth is the Muslim's ablution and suffices him in place of water
babs.6: If the junub fears illness, death or thirst, he performs tayammum

334.matn: ʿAbdullāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, she said: “We set out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on one of his journeys. When we were at al-Baydāʾ or Dhāt al-Jaysh, a necklace of mine broke. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed to search for it, and the people stayed with him, and they were not at any water. The people came to Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq and said: Do you not see what ʿĀʾisha has done? She has detained the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people, and they are not at any water, and they have no water with them. Abū Bakr came while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had put his head on my thigh and fallen asleep, and said: You have detained the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people, and they are not at any water, and they have no water with them. ʿĀʾisha said: Abū Bakr reproached me and said what Allah willed him to say, and he began poking me in the side with his hand. Nothing prevented me from moving except the place of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on my thigh. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose at dawn with no water, and Allah revealed the verse of tayammum, and they performed tayammum. Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr said: This is not the first of your blessings, O family of Abū Bakr. She said: Then we made the camel I had been on rise, and found the necklace beneath it.”
334.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith stands at the beginning of the Book of Tayammum, before the first chapter. ʿĀʾisha reports that a necklace of hers broke on a journey and the Prophet stayed with the people to search for it although they were at no water. Abū Bakr reproached her, but she stayed still because the Prophet’s head lay on her thigh. At dawn Allah revealed the verse of tayammum, and the people performed tayammum. Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr said this was not the first blessing of the family of Abū Bakr. At the end it is mentioned that the necklace was found beneath the camel.

335.matn: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us (change of chain). He said: And Saʿīd ibn an-Naḍr narrated to me, he said: Hushaym informed us, he said: Sayyār informed us, he said: Yazīd – that is Ibn Ṣuhayb al-Faqīr – narrated to us, he said: Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh informed us that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given five things that were not given to anyone before me: I was made victorious through terror at a distance of a month’s journey; the earth was made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, so whichever man of my community is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray; war booty was made lawful for me and was not lawful for anyone before me; I was given intercession; and a prophet used to be sent only to his own people, whereas I was sent to all people.”
335.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith stands at the beginning of the Book of Tayammum, before the first chapter. Jābir reports that the Prophet named five things given to him and to no one before him: victory through terror at a month’s distance, the earth as a place of prayer and a means of purification, the lawfulness of war booty, intercession, and being sent to all people rather than to one people only. The chain gives two routes of transmission from Hushaym onward.

336.matn: Zakariyyāʾ ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated to us, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: “She had borrowed a necklace from Asmāʾ, and it was lost. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent a man, and he found it. Then the time of prayer overtook them and they had no water, so they prayed. They complained of that to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Allah revealed the verse of tayammum. Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr said to ʿĀʾisha: May Allah reward you with good! By Allah, nothing befell you that you disliked, but Allah made good in it for you and for the Muslims.”
336.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “When one finds neither water nor earth.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the necklace she had borrowed from Asmāʾ was lost and the Prophet sent a man to search, who found it. The time of prayer overtook the people and they had no water, so they prayed. When they complained of this to the Prophet, Allah revealed the verse of tayammum. Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr then made a prayer of blessing for ʿĀʾisha.

337.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿa, from al-Aʿraj, he said: I heard ʿUmayr, the freedman of Ibn ʿAbbās, say: “I came together with ʿAbdullāh ibn Yasār, the freedman of Maymūna, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and we entered upon Abū l-Juhaym ibn al-Ḥārith ibn aṣ-Ṣimma al-Anṣārī. Abū l-Juhaym said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was coming from the direction of the well of Jamal. A man met him and greeted him, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not return his greeting until he turned to the wall, wiped his face and hands on it, and then returned the greeting, peace be upon him.”
337.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Tayammum at one’s residence when one finds no water and fears missing the prayer.” Abū l-Juhaym reports that the Prophet was coming from the direction of the well of Jamal and a man greeted him. The Prophet returned the greeting only after turning to the wall and wiping his face and hands on it.

338.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, Al-Ḥakam narrated to us, from Dharr, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from his father, he said: “A man came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said: I became junub and found no water? ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: Do you not remember that we were on a journey, you and I? You did not pray, while I rolled in the dust and prayed. I mentioned it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: It would have sufficed you to do just this. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, struck the earth with his two palms, blew into them, and wiped his face and palms with them.”
338.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Does the one performing tayammum blow on his hands?” Saʿīd’s father reports that a man who was junub and found no water came to ʿUmar. ʿAmmār reminds ʿUmar of a shared journey on which ʿUmar did not pray, while he rolled in the dust and prayed. The Prophet told him it would have sufficed to do so, struck the earth with both palms, blew into them, and wiped his face and palms.

339.matn: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba informed us: Al-Ḥakam informed me, from Dharr, from (Saʿīd) ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from his father: ʿAmmār said it thus. And Shuʿba struck the earth with his hands, then brought them to his mouth, then wiped his face and palms. And an-Naḍr said: Shuʿba informed us, from al-Ḥakam, he said: I heard Dharr say, from Ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā. Al-Ḥakam said: And I also heard it from Ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from his father, he said: ʿAmmār said.
339.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Tayammum for the face and hands.” The entry refers with “thus” to ʿAmmār’s wording in the previous hadith. It describes how Shuʿba demonstrated the act: he struck the earth with his hands, brought them to his mouth, and then wiped his face and palms. It also gives a chain variant from an-Naḍr, and al-Ḥakam adds that he also heard the hadith directly from Ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān.

340.matn: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Dharr, from Ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from his father, that he was present with ʿUmar when ʿAmmār said to him: We were on a raid and became junub. And he said: “He spat lightly into them both.”
340.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Tayammum for the face and hands.” The father of Ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān reports that he was present when ʿAmmār told ʿUmar that they had become junub on a raid. The entry also gives the wording that the Prophet spat lightly into his hands; the rest of the text is not written out.

341.matn: Muḥammad ibn Kathīr narrated to us: Shuʿba informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Dharr, from Ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, he said: “ʿAmmār said to ʿUmar: I rolled in the dust, then I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: The face and the palms suffice you.”
341.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Tayammum for the face and hands.” ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān reports that ʿAmmār told ʿUmar that he had rolled in the dust and then come to the Prophet, who told him that the face and palms sufficed.

342.matn: Muslim narrated to us, Shuʿba narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Dharr, from Ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, he said: I was present with ʿUmar, and ʿAmmār said to him: – and he went on to relate the hadith.
342.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the entry under the same chapter “Tayammum for the face and hands.” ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān reports that he was present when ʿAmmār spoke to ʿUmar. The wording is not written out here but only continued with the note that the hadith was passed on.

343.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Ghundar narrated to us: Shuʿba narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Dharr, from Ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from his father, he said: ʿAmmār said: “Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, struck the earth with his hand and wiped his face and palms.”
343.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Tayammum for the face and hands.” ʿAmmār reports that the Prophet struck the earth with his hand and wiped his face and palms with it.

344.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to me, he said: ʿAwf narrated to us, he said: Abū Rajāʾ narrated to us, from ʿImrān, he said: “We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey, and we travelled by night until, near the end of the night, we lay down – and there is no sleep sweeter to a traveller than that. Nothing woke us but the heat of the sun. The first to wake was so-and-so, then so-and-so, then so-and-so – Abū Rajāʾ named them but ʿAwf forgot – and fourth was ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he slept, was not woken until he woke by himself, for we did not know what happened to him in his sleep. When ʿUmar woke and saw what had befallen the people – and he was a robust man – he said the takbīr and raised his voice with it. He did not cease saying the takbīr and raising his voice until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, woke at his voice. When he woke, they complained to him of what had befallen them. He said: No harm – or: It will not harm. Set off! He set off, travelled a short distance, then dismounted, called for water for ablution and performed ablution. The call to prayer was made, and he led the people in prayer. When he turned from his prayer, there was a man standing apart who had not prayed with the people. He said: What prevented you, so-and-so, from praying with the people? He said: Janāba befell me and there is no water. He said: Keep to clean earth; it suffices you. Then the Prophet travelled on, and the people complained to him of thirst. He dismounted and called so-and-so – Abū Rajāʾ named him, ʿAwf forgot – and called ʿAlī and said: Go and look for water. They went and met a woman between two water-skins, or two water containers, of water on a camel of hers. They asked her: Where is the water? She said: My last contact with water was yesterday at this hour, and our men are away. They said to her: Then come along. She said: Where to? They said: To the Messenger of Allah. She said: The one who is called the Ṣābiʾ? They said: He is the one you mean; so come along. They brought her to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and told him the matter. He said: Make her get down from her camel. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a vessel and poured into it from the mouths of the two water-skins or containers, tied their mouths and loosened the lower spouts. It was announced among the people: Give water and take water! So whoever wished gave water, and whoever wished drew water. At the end of that he gave the one on whom janāba had befallen a vessel of water and said: Go and pour it over yourself. She stood watching what was done with her water. By Allah, they stopped drawing from it, and it seemed to us that it was fuller than when they began. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Gather for her. They gathered for her ʿAjwa dates, flour and roasted-barley meal until they had gathered food for her, put it in a cloth, lifted her onto her camel and placed the cloth before her. He said to her: You know that we have taken nothing from your water, but Allah is the One who gave us to drink. She came to her people, who had missed her. They said: What kept you, so-and-so? She said: A wonder: two men met me and took me to this man who is called the Ṣābiʾ, and he did such and such. By Allah, he is the greatest magician between this and this – and she raised her two fingers, the middle and the index, to the sky, meaning heaven and earth – or he is truly the Messenger of Allah. After that the Muslims raided the polytheists around her, but did not harm the encampment she belonged to. One day she said to her people: I think these people are leaving you alone on purpose. Do you want Islam? They obeyed her and entered Islam.”
344.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Clean earth is the ablution of the Muslim and suffices him in place of water.” ʿImrān reports a night journey on which the group was woken only by the heat of the sun, and ʿUmar’s takbīr by which the Prophet woke. After setting off and performing ablution the Prophet led the prayer; to a man standing apart who was junub and had no water he said that clean earth sufficed him. Water was then sought, a woman with two water containers was found, and the water sufficed for everyone; the man was given water to pour over himself and the woman was given provisions. She told her people, and in the end they entered Islam. The entry names some people only as “so-and-so” because the narrator had forgotten them.
